subject: Oxbridge Clinic - pharmacy integration PHI scope, retention, and BAA timeline
messages:
From: Laura Emerson <laura@oxbridgeclinic.org>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Dr. Samir Patel <s.patel@oxbridgeclinic.org>, procurement@oxbridgeclinic.org
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Oxbridge RFP - PHI scope for pharmacy integration and BAA timeline

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our RFP review for adding LLM-assisted medication reconciliation (pharmacy integration), we need clearer answers on the following PHI handling points so our security and legal teams can greenlight next steps: 

- Exact PHI elements that would be transmitted to Redwood during inference (e.g., patient name, DOB, medication list, pharmacy IDs).
- Whether we can scope calls so prescription identifiers are tokenized/masked before leaving our network.
- Data retention defaults for inference logs and how long deidentified vs identifiable artifacts are kept.
- Encryption at rest and in transit specifics, and whether our HSM/KMS can be used (we prefer using our cloud KMS).
- Availability of audit logs and sample log formats for access reviews and incident response.

We're also syncing legal and procurement on the BAA: what's your estimated timeline for providing a signed BAA draft and are there any standard carve-outs we should expect? I attached Section B of our RFP for context.

Can we target a short technical call next week to walk through the data flow? Our team is available Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Thanks,
Laura Emerson
Director of IT Procurement
Oxbridge Clinic
(attachment: Oxbridge_RFP_SectionB.pdf)

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Emerson <laura@oxbridgeclinic.org>
Cc: Dr. Samir Patel <s.patel@oxbridgeclinic.org>, procurement@oxbridgeclinic.org
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Oxbridge RFP - PHI scope for pharmacy integration and BAA timeline

Hi Laura — great questions, thanks for the RFP snippet. I wanted to provide an initial technical QA and propose next steps; I'll loop in our security and legal for specifics on the BAA draft. High-level answers below; we can expand on any item on the call.

1) PHI elements transmitted to Redwood during inference
   - Typical payloads for the medication reconciliation flow include patient identifier (customer-assigned ID), medication name(s), dosage strings, and free-text clinician notes.
   - Names/DOB are optional — customers can remove or pseudonymize them before calling the API. We recommend sending a non-reversible patient token where possible.

2) Tokenization / scoping options
   - We support client-side tokenization best practice. Additionally, our SDKs include hooks to mask fields prior to transmission. If Oxbridge prefers, we can implement a middleware rule to zero-out PHI fields on your side before outbound calls.

3) Data retention and logs
   - Hosted default: inference request metadata retained for 30 days; full request/response payloads are retained for 7 days and then purged unless customer enables longer retention.
   - We offer an enterprise retention configuration (0/7/30/90/365 days) for Dedicated/Private customers. For PHI workloads we recommend either 0 or 7-day retention.

4) Encryption and KMS/HSM options
   - In transit: TLS 1.2+ mandatory.
   - At rest: AES-256 for persisted artifacts.
   - KMS: For Private and Dedicated deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For hosted tier we can arrange a KMS integration discussion with your security team.

5) Audit logs and evidence
   - We provide access logs, model invocation traces, and administrator action logs. Sample log schemas and a redacted example can be shared; Rishi (security) will attach an evidence packet.

BAA timeline and next steps
   - Legal: we can provide a draft BAA within 3 business days upon receipt of Oxbridge contact details for execution (we typically redline once and target signing within 2 weeks for standard terms). Any carve-outs should be called out in advance (e.g., on-prem data residency constraints).

Suggested next steps:
- Schedule 30-min tech walkthrough (Tue/Wed morning PST works) — propose Tue 8:30am PST.
- I will loop in Rishi (security) and Marissa (sales ops/legal) to surface the sample logs and a BAA draft.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sofia / team — attaching the evidence packet and drafting quick clarifications for Oxbridge. I also added a short FAQ at the top of the packet to speed review.

Clarifications for Oxbridge (to include in the tech call):
- Our recommended minimum for PHI workloads on hosted tier is 7-day payload retention with customer-side tokenization; Dedicated/Private supports 0-day retention (no payload persisted) if you route inference through your VPC and enable our stateless mode.
- Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated/Private; for hosted customers we can set up envelope encryption with customer keys but full KMS integration requires a Dedicated plan.
- Audit logs: we provide immutable access logs for admin actions for 12 months (configurable), invocation logs for 90 days by default (configurable down to 0). We can deliver a redacted sample in CSV/JSON.
- Subprocessors: standard list attached; any required exclusion needs to be highlighted before final BAA.

Attachments included: BAA_Draft_v1.docx (redline-ready), redwood_encryption_kms_diagram.png, oxbridge_sample_logs_redacted.csv

I'll be on the Tue 8:30am PST call and can walk through the evidence and persistence options.

-Rishi
